dishes.name: Beshbarmak
dishes.description: Beshbarmak (Kyrgyz: бешбармак, romanized: beşbarmak; Bashkir: бишбармаҡ, romanized: bişbarmaq; lit. 'five fingers') is a meat, noodles, and onion broth dish in Central Asian cuisine.

dishes.name: Kazy
dishes.description: Kazy (Kazakh: Қазы; Russian: Казы) is a salt lake in Akkuly District, Pavlodar Region, Kazakhstan.

dishes.name: Baursak
dishes.description: Boortsog, boorsoq, baursak, baursaq, bauyrsaq, borsok, or boorsok is a fried dough food found in the cuisines of Central Asia, Idel-Ural, Mongolia, and the Middle East.

dishes.name: Kuyrdak
dishes.description: Kuurdak (Kazakh: қуырдақ, quyrdaq, Kyrgyz: куурдак, Turkmen: gowurdak; Говурдак, Uyghur: قورداق қордақ qordaq, Uzbek: qovurdoq, Mongolian: Хуурдаг), transliterated with various spellings, is a traditional meat dish made in Central Asia.

dishes.name: Kumis
dishes.description: Kumis ( KOO-mis, rarely KUM-is), alternatively spelled coumis or kumyz, also known as airag ( EYE-rag), is a traditional fermented dairy product made from mare milk.

dishes.name: Shubat
dishes.description: Chal, also shubat or khoormog, is a Turkic (especially Turkmen, Uzbek and Kazakh) and Mongolic beverage of fermented camel milk, sparkling white with a sour flavor, popular in Central Asia — particularly in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. In Kazakhstan the drink is known as shubat, and is a staple summer food.
